title: Spiced Apple Cake with Caramel Sauce
story: This is autumn in a cake pan. The spice blend isn't subtle — it's the whole point. The grated apples disappear into the crumb as they bake, leaving moisture and flavor behind without a single chunk to interrupt the texture. The caramel sauce is the kind of finish that makes the difference between a good cake and one people talk about.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
2 cups peeled and grated apple (about 2 medium apples)

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp nutmeg, ¼ tsp ginger, ¼ tsp allspice, and ½ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter and 1 cup granulated sugar together until light and creamy, about 3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look pale and fluffy — this builds the cake's lift.

steps.text: Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each before adding the next.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract and ½ cup whole milk.
Fold in 2 cups peeled and grated apple. If using ½ cup pecans, fold them in now as well. The batter will look wet — that's correct, the apples add significant moisture.
Add the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.

steps.donenessCue: A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with a few dry crumbs. The apple moisture in this batter means it may need the full 40 minutes — don't pull it early based on the top color alone.

steps.text: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Drizzle with caramel sauce just before serving. If serving a group, pour caramel over the whole cake; if serving over time, keep the sauce on the side so it doesn't make the top soggy.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Make a quick caramel sauce: cook 1 cup granulated sugar in a dry pan over medium heat, swirling (not stirring) until deep amber. Remove from heat, carefully whisk in ½ cup warm heavy cream, then 2 tbsp butter and a pinch of salt. It keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks.
Toast the pecans in a dry skillet for 3 minutes before folding in — the spice mix already perfumes the kitchen, toasted pecans take it further.
Add a pinch of black pepper to the dry ingredients. It's invisible in the finished cake but makes every other spice taste more like itself.
Serve warm slices with vanilla ice cream and the caramel sauce poured over both — the contrast of cold ice cream and warm cake is the point.
Use a mix of apple varieties: one tart (Granny Smith) and one sweet (Honeycrisp) for more complex flavor.
storage: Store loosely covered at room temperature for up to 4 days — the apple content keeps this cake moist longer than most. Refrigerate for up to 1 week. Store caramel sauce separately and add at serving time. Freeze unglazed cake for up to 3 months.
